messages:
sarah-wu: Quick follow-up from the segmented pool RFC — we still need to pick a concrete boundary/contract between the small-object slab allocator and the segmented/offload pool. I sketched a practical heuristic: size threshold + age + hotness score. Want to converge on an interface we can ship as a canary. @rajiv @nate any blockers?

rajiv: I like the hybrid heuristic. Main concern is migration cost (device <-> host) and how we measure "hotness". We should avoid oscillation (promote/demote thrash). Suggest we track a simple EWMA of accesses per allocation and only promote when EWMA > X for Y windows. Also need a cancellation window: once promoted don't demote for Z seconds unless memory pressure is high.

nate: Agree re: oscillation. Also need to factor DMA setup cost for pinned host staging vs GPU-local pages. Rough rule: don't promote allocations < 64KB because the transfer overhead and PCIe latency will dominate. For larger chunks (>1MB) we should prefer direct pinned allocations in device memory.

olga: On fragmentation vs migration: compaction can reduce long-term fragmentation but is expensive. Proposal: do lightweight migration for hot large objects, and run a periodic background compactor that triggers only when fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 and gpu_util < 0.6. Pseudocode: ```if fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 and gpu_util < 0.6: run_compaction_pass(timeout_ms=200)``` This keeps compaction opportunistic.

rajiv: We also need telemetry + safety knobs. Add counters: migration_attempts, migration_success, migration_cost_ms (histogram), post_migration_latency_p50/p95. And a hard-config knob to disable promotion per-tenant for Private deployments.

emily: For private deploys we need backward compatibility — simplest is a config flag in the agent: "allocator.experimental_segmented_pool = true|false" and runtime-exposed per-tenant thresholds. That lets us roll feature-gated canary.

sarah-wu: Good. For the API surface I'm proposing two small primitives on the allocator interface so runtime and model-serving code can coordinate: 1) allocation.metadata.attach({"alloc_class": "hot|cold|pinned", "evict_priority": 0..255}) 2) allocator.promote_hint(ptr, expected_size, reason_tags) That keeps the heavy decision logic in the allocator but lets runtime provide hints. Example: ```alloc.metadata.attach({"alloc_class":"hot","evict_priority":32}) allocator.promote_hint(ptr, 1<<20, {"reason":"kvcache_hot"})```

nate: API looks fine. Make promote_hint best-effort and async — return immediately with a ticket id so caller can poll or register a callback. If promotion fails we shouldn't block inference.

olga: On compaction internals: prefer in-place migrate-to-free-list when possible to avoid extra allocations; use a bounded worker pool so compaction doesn't steal all GPU bandwidth. Also keep a migration credit system per-stream to limit concurrent DMA.

rajiv: Operationally: we should gate the rollout behind two telemetry gates: (1) migration_cost_ms p95 < 5ms on synthetic workload, and (2) no increase in 99th percentile end-to-end request latency in canary by > 1%. If either fails auto-disable promotion.

devops-bot: Created INF-3124: "segmented-pool promotion canary + telemetry" and assigned to @sarah-wu.

emily: Small nit — document the default thresholds in the config schema and mark them as adjustable via Redwood Console for Hosted customers.

sarah-wu: I'll draft a minimal RFC patch with API signatures, default thresholds (size_promote_threshold=64KB, promote_ewma_window=8s, demote_cooldown=30s, compaction_threshold=0.25) and telemetry hooks. Will put perf microbench results in the PR. If no objections I'll open by EOD. :thumbsup:

rajiv: :thumbsup: sounds good. I'll add the telemetry dashboards and a test harness.

nate: I'll run DMA transfer microbench across a few GPUs and upload numbers to the PR.

olga: I'll prototype the bounded compaction worker and migration crediting in a branch.

sarah-wu: Thanks all — let's keep the initial canary conservative and iterate.
